title: Safety signs and symbols
summary: Explains the four categories of safety sign and their colours, examples of each, and how CLP regulations replaced CHIP for hazardous substance labelling.

sections.heading: Why safety signs are used
paragraphs: If a hazard cannot be adequately controlled by any other means, it must be marked with a safety sign. Employers must make sure employees are trained in what safety signs mean.
bullets: Signs are used when a hazard cannot be controlled by other means
Employers must train employees in the meaning of safety signs
Emergency escape routes and firefighting equipment must have their locations identified with safety signs

sections.heading: The four categories and their colours
paragraphs: Safety signs are grouped into four categories, each with its own colour scheme. There are also location signs for firefighting equipment.

sections.heading: Examples of each sign type
paragraphs: Each category has familiar examples that you should be able to recognise.
bullets: Information (advisory): fire exit, first aid, fire assembly point
Mandatory: safety helmet must be worn, ear protection must be worn, eye protection must be worn
Prohibition: no smoking, do not extinguish with water, no unauthorised persons

sections.heading: Hazardous substances: CHIP and CLP
paragraphs: The Chemical Hazard Information and Packaging for Supply (CHIP) Regulations have been replaced by the Classification, Labelling and Packaging (CLP) Regulations. Materials manufactured before June 2015 may still use the old CHIP labelling until 2017.
CLP uses visual signage to help people appreciate the dangers of chemicals in the work environment.
bullets: CHIP replaced by CLP (Classification, Labelling and Packaging)
Materials manufactured before June 2015 may still use CHIP labelling until 2017

flashcards.front: When must a hazard be marked with a safety sign?
flashcards.back: If it cannot be adequately controlled by any other means.

flashcards.front: What must every employer do about safety signs?
flashcards.back: Ensure their employees are trained in the meaning of safety signs.

flashcards.front: What must be identified with safety signs in an emergency context?
flashcards.back: The locations of emergency escape routes and firefighting equipment.

flashcards.front: How many categories of safety sign are there, and what are they?
flashcards.back: Four: warning, information, mandatory and prohibition signs. There are also location signs for firefighting equipment.

flashcards.front: Give three examples of information (advisory) signs.
flashcards.back: Fire exit, first aid and fire assembly point.

flashcards.front: Give three examples of prohibition signs.
flashcards.back: No smoking, do not extinguish with water and no unauthorised persons.

flashcards.front: Give three examples of mandatory signs.
flashcards.back: Safety helmet must be worn, ear protection must be worn and eye protection must be worn.
The Classification, Labelling and Packaging (CLP) Regulations.

quiz.q: What colour scheme do prohibition signs use?
What colour scheme do mandatory signs use?
What colour scheme do warning signs use?
Which category of sign is a fire exit sign?
quiz.why: Fire exit, first aid and fire assembly point are information (advisory) signs.

quiz.q: A sign reading 'Safety helmet must be worn' belongs to which category?
quiz.why: Safety helmet, ear protection and eye protection signs are mandatory signs.

quiz.q: A 'No smoking' sign belongs to which category?
quiz.why: No smoking is one of the prohibition signs.
